idea_name: Engle-Granger and Johansen cointegration as multi-asset equilibrium regime sensors
mechanism: Engle-Granger coint() on a pair yields p-value and OLS hedge ratio for a two-asset mean-reverting spread; Johansen coint_johansen on N log-price series yields trace/max-eigen stats vs critical values to infer cointegration rank and the first eigenvector as portfolio weights. Rank>=1 marks an equilibrium regime where a linear combination of prices is stationary even if individuals are not.
data_needed: Aligned close (or log-close) series for 2+ symbols; sample length large enough for Johansen (author switches D1→H1 when short); det_order and k_ar_diff settings
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY/AUDUSD/USDCAD/NZDUSD/USDCHF D1 ~600 days; NVDA/GOOGL H1; USDCAD-NZDUSD; XAUEUR/XAUUSD context
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a basket-level equilibrium-regime label (cointegrated vs not, and how many independent stationary spreads) beyond single-asset trend/vol states.
quote: Correlation captures only short-term relationships, while cointegration captures equilibrium relationships in the long run. Two variables can be highly correlated but not cointegrated, and vice versa.

idea_name: ADF+KPSS dual-test spread stationarity regime gate
mechanism: After forming the cointegrated residual/spread, run ADF (null=unit root) and KPSS (null=stationarity). Four-case interpretation: both agree stationary → tradeable mean-reversion; both agree non-stationary → reject; KPSS stationary + ADF non-stationary → trend-stationary (detrend); KPSS non-stationary + ADF stationary → difference-stationary. Dual agreement is required before treating the spread as a valid sensing/trading state.
data_needed: Spread series from EG residual or Johansen P·w; adfuller and kpss from statsmodels
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NVDA/GOOGL H1 spreads; USDCAD-NZDUSD D1 spread
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat dual ADF/KPSS agreement as a hard gate on whether a relative-value regime is still mean-reverting rather than relying on a single unit-root test.
quote: Case 4: KPSS indicates non-stationarity and ADF indicates stationarity - The series is difference stationary. Differencing is to be used to make series stationary.

idea_name: Multivariate Johansen-spread z-score as basket volatility sensor
mechanism: Build spread = Σ w_i·price_i from Johansen first eigenvector; maintain a rolling lookback buffer of spread values; compute MA and StdDev; enter when |spread−mean| > EntryThreshold·σ and exit when back inside ExitThreshold·σ. Spread σ is the live volatility of the cointegrated residual, not of any single leg.
data_needed: Live multi-symbol ticks/bars; Johansen weights; LookbackPeriod for MA/σ; EntryThreshold/ExitThreshold in σ units
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MU/NVDA/MPWR/MCHP; D1 cointegration, operable on H1; EntryThreshold=2.0, ExitThreshold=0.3, LookbackPeriod=252 default; also AAAU/USGO/BGLD and CEF/SLV/SIVR D1 examples
why_new_for_mis: Provides a market-neutral residual-volatility sensor for a sector basket—MIS can track when relative mispricing volatility expands/contracts independently of directional market vol.
quote: Our sample implementation starts by defining thresholds for entry/exit points in the form of standard deviations from the mean.

idea_name: Timer-driven multi-symbol quote sync for residual sensing
mechanism: Because OnTick is bound to the chart symbol, the EA uses EventSetTimer(1s) to actively poll all basket symbols, recompute spread/mean/σ outside the tick handler, avoiding silent desync when one leg stops ticking. High-liquidity legs are preferred so the residual sensor stays time-aligned.
data_needed: SymbolInfoTick for each basket leg on a fixed timer; liquidity filter so legs do not drift out of sync >~seconds
why_new_for_mis: Frames multi-asset residual sensing as an active sync problem—MIS multi-leg sensors need a timer/poll architecture, not single-symbol tick binding.
quote: By using a timer, in this case with a one-second interval, we can be sure that at this interval we will check for new quotes. We are moving from a passive quote updating to an active quote updating.

idea_name: Cointegration non-persistence as continuous regime-change premise
mechanism: Article states cointegration is not guaranteed to persist: management, macro, or sector shocks can destroy an existing relationship or create a new one at any time; portfolio weights also drift continuously. Sensing pipeline must therefore re-test cointegration and refresh weights on a schedule, and halt trading when the model is invalid.
data_needed: Persistent OHLCV DB; scheduled re-runs of Johansen/EG/ADF/KPSS; strategy table for live EA parameter refresh
why_new_for_mis: Treats cointegration itself as a perishable regime whose death is a first-class change event MIS must monitor, not a one-time filter.
quote: However, two or more assets may have been cointegrated for the last two years and start losing cointegration tomorrow. That is, there is no guarantee that a cointegrated pair or group of assets will remain cointegrated.

idea_name: Multi-lookback multi-timeframe Pearson correlation evolution sensor
mechanism: Store Pearson r(ref, candidate) for each (timeframe, lookback) in corr_pearson; compare how coefficient evolves across 252/180/120/90/60/30-day windows and across H4 vs D1. Rising/falling r across nested windows is a co-movement regime map used before cointegration tests—not as a substitute for them.
data_needed: Price panels per TF; lookback grid; ref ticker (NVDA); SQLite corr_pearson with (tstamp, ref, corr, tf, lookback, coefficient)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: ~63 Nasdaq semiconductor stocks vs NVDA; H4 and D1; AVGO–NVDA year-to-month lookback evolution example
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a structured co-movement surface over (TF×lookback) rather than a single correlation number—useful for detecting when short-horizon co-movement decouples from long-horizon structure.
quote: By calculating correlation in short timeframes and short lookback periods, while at the same time testing for cointegration in long timeframes and lookback periods.

idea_name: Average real-volume liquidity eliminator and relative liquidity rank
mechanism: SQL AVG(real_volume) per ticker over stored bars ranks semiconductor names; low-liquidity names are eliminatory because illiquid legs widen spreads and desync residual calculation. For FX, substitute tick_volume. Round-trip cost approximated (~0.1% of traded value) as a companion tradability filter.
data_needed: market_data.real_volume (stocks) or tick_volume (FX); symbol metadata; optional spread snapshots
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: 63 Nasdaq semiconductor symbols; NVDA highest volume; H4 scoring runs on top-10 liquid names
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes liquidity as a hard MIS gate on multi-leg residual sensors, not only as a cost overlay.
quote: Liquidity is an indispensable criterion because spreads involving illiquid stocks may be costly to trade. We need reasonable spreads, and not only for stat arb.

idea_name: Unified cointegration rank_score from EG p-value and Johansen max eigenvalue
mechanism: For pairs, rank_score = −p_value (Engle-Granger); for baskets, rank_score = max eigenvalue (Johansen), with strength_stat = ADF score (EG) or max trace (Johansen). Sort descending to rank strongest equilibrium relationships across mixed pair/basket candidates on a common scale; also store eigen_strength separately as tightness of the strongest vector.
data_needed: All 2/3/4-combinations of liquid symbols; per (tf, lookback) coint runs written to coint_rank
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Top-10 liquid semiconductors; H4; 60–180 day lookbacks; baskets including NVDA/INTC/AVGO/ASX
why_new_for_mis: Turns cointegration diagnostics into a comparable regime-strength score MIS can rank and threshold across the universe.
quote: df["rank_score"] = df.apply(lambda row: -row["p_value"] if row["method"] == "Engle-Granger" else row["eigen_strength"], axis=1)

idea_name: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck half-life of spread mean reversion
mechanism: Model stationary spread as AR(1)/OU: regress Δspread on lagged spread; if β<0, half_life = −ln(2)/β (in bars of the test TF); β≥0 → ∞ (non-reverting). Filter baskets to a strategy-aligned band (e.g. 1–5 H4 bars ≈4–20h for swing H4). Infinite/NaN half-life eliminates the candidate.
data_needed: Stationary Johansen/EG spread; OLS via statsmodels; half_life column in coint_rank
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Semiconductor baskets on H4; examples ~1.5 bars (~6h) to ~934 bars (~155 days); INTC/AMD/AVGO/MU backtest
why_new_for_mis: Quantifies expected reversion speed of a relative-value residual—a timing/vol-of-mispricing sensor MIS can use to match holding-horizon regimes.
quote: The half-life of mean reversion quantifies the expected time for the spread (the residual from the cointegrating relationship) to revert halfway back to its mean after the deviation.

idea_name: In-sample/out-of-sample ADF stability_stat for hedge-ratio robustness
mechanism: Split prices 70/30; estimate cointegration vector on IS; apply same vector to OOS prices to form spread; return OOS ADF statistic as stability_stat. More negative than ~−2.86 (5%) ⇒ vector still produces a stationary spread on unseen data; near-zero/positive ⇒ unstable relationship demoted in scoring.
data_needed: Price panel length ≥~50 (≥30 OOS bars); EG or Johansen vector; adfuller on OOS spread
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H4 semiconductor baskets; 120-day lookback example; filter stability_stat < −2.86
why_new_for_mis: Converts hedge-ratio fragility into a forward-looking stationarity score—MIS can demand OOS residual stationarity before trusting an equilibrium regime.
quote: It is the ADF statistic computed on the out-of-sample spread that tests whether the spread remains stationary when the cointegration vector (derived from in-sample data) is applied to unseen data.

idea_name: Rolling Windows Eigenvector Comparison (RWEC) cosine-angle drift sensor
mechanism: Re-estimate Johansen cointegration vectors on rolling windows (e.g. window=252, step=22); compute cosine similarity / angle in degrees between successive normalized eigenvectors; flag unstable when angle exceeds threshold (e.g. 30°). High temporal resolution pinpoints when hedge structure flips (sign changes, weight inversions). Pair with walk-forward IS/OOS ADF for spread stationarity.
data_needed: Rolling multi-asset price windows; Johansen evec per window; cosine distance series; stability threshold in degrees
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GLD/GDX, EEM/VWO, XLK/AAA ETF pairs D1 ~2000 bars; also applicable to stock baskets; H4 live-monitor framing
why_new_for_mis: Direct structural-change sensor on the hedge map itself—MIS gets timed alerts when relative-value geometry breaks, not only when residual ADF fails later.
quote: While the IS/OOS ADF gives us no clue about the point in time when the cointegration was lost, the RWEC shows it precisely. This property, called high temporal resolution, is one of the main reasons that make it so useful for live trading monitoring.

idea_name: Walk-forward OOS ADF success-rate as live signal-stability monitor
mechanism: Instead of one IS/OOS split, roll the split forward (e.g. train_frac=0.7, oos_length=100, step=22 trading days); record OOS ADF p-value stationarity per window; aggregate OOS success rate, mean/median p-value. Divergent mean vs median flags outlier break windows; falling success rate is an early live-monitor risk signal.
data_needed: Long price history (~2000 bars); overlapping WF schedule; per-window ADF p-values and betas
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: XLK/AAA D1; 9 WF windows example with 55.6% OOS success rate
why_new_for_mis: Turns residual stationarity into a rolling reliability metric MIS can watch as a regime-health time series.
quote: The difference is telling us that this mean was highly affected by outlier values. In our case, outlier values are peaks where the stationarity was lost, but the median ensures that most of the time the spread was stationary.

idea_name: RWEC step-size as structural-break detection resolution control
mechanism: Backtests show overlapping step length controls when cointegration failure is visible: n_bars≈594, window=90, step=22 → 18% relative DD; same with step=5 → 85% DD but ~5× more points that reveal a structural break missed by the coarser step. Window length vs step trades turnover/noise against break-detection latency.
data_needed: Timestamped RWEC weight updates; backtest aligned to update tstamps; relative drawdown as evaluation criterion
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: INTC/AMD/AVGO/MU H4; RWEC 504+90 bars; windows 90 vs 45; steps 22 vs 5
why_new_for_mis: Shows MIS that change-sensor cadence (step) is itself a sensing hyperparameter: too coarse misses breaks; too fine amplifies noise and turnover.
quote: When we reduced our step from one trading month (22 days) to one trading week (5 days), we degraded our results dramatically from 18.8% to 85.11%. However, by having nearly five times more data points, from 23 to 101, we also spotted a failure in the cointegration.

idea_name: Chow test confirmatory structural-break sensor on pair beta
mechanism: Given a hypothesized break date, run OLS on pre-break, post-break, and full-sample (restricted) regressions of Y on X; Chow F = [(SSR_full−(SSR_pre+SSR_post))/k] / [(SSR_pre+SSR_post)/(N−2k)]; p<0.05 rejects no-break. Distinguishes slope inversion (beta sign flip) from intercept shift (parallel gap). Needs ~20–30 post-break bars for practical power; pairs only.
data_needed: Paired price series; candidate breakpoint date; OLS SSRs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NVDA/INTC breakpoint 2025-09-18 (F≈568.7, beta −2.59→+0.95); US500/JPN225 breakpoint 2025-04-02 (intercept-shift break, F≈57.5)
why_new_for_mis: Supplies a confirmatory regime-break test MIS can fire after RWEC/news suspicion—separates permanent parameter change from noise.
quote: an unexpected change over time in the parameters of regression models

idea_name: Recursive CUSUM of regression residuals as early structural-break alarm
mechanism: Fit RecursiveLS(Y, [1,X]); track cusum of residuals vs 5% boundary (~0.948·(√n + 2n/√n)); alarm when |cusum| exceeds the tunnel. Continuous/recursive—unlike Chow which needs a preset date and post-break buffer—so it can fire within ~1 bar of a priced-in shock after residual errors accumulate.
data_needed: Streaming or expanding pair prices; statsmodels RecursiveLS; critical bound at 95%
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NVDA/INTC D1 Jun–Dec 2025; CRITICAL SIGNAL on 2025-09-19 (day after partnership announcement)
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a real-time residual-accumulation break alarm that can precede confirmatory Chow and catch anticipated corporate/macro regime shifts as they embed in prices.
quote: CRITICAL SIGNAL on 2025-09-19 The model has deviated beyond the 95% confidence interval.

idea_name: Pearson correlation sign-flip as discrete co-movement regime switch
mechanism: Compare Pearson r over pre-event vs post-event windows: NVDA/INTC went from r≈−0.71 (competitors, opposite moves) to r≈+0.75 (partners, same-direction moves) around the Sep 2025 partnership—absolute strength similar, sign inverted. Any portfolio using stable beta must recalibrate or stop. RWEC angles rose from ~0° to >150° around the same event.
data_needed: Paired closes; pre/post event windows; Pearson matrix; optional RWEC accompaniment
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NVDA/INTC D1 Jan 2024–Sep 2025 vs Sep–Dec 2025; RWEC H4 504-day lookback
why_new_for_mis: Defines a crisp MIS change event: correlation-sign regime switch, distinct from mere |r| decay—critical for hedge-direction sensors.
quote: Until the week before the announcement, there was a negative correlation between NVDA and INTC... After the partnership announcement, the correlation was flipped... positive correlation of 0.75.
